description:
AI-powered research assistant for your Zotero library

RAG Assistant for Zotero is an AI-powered research assistant that lets you
chat with your Zotero library using natural language. It uses retrieval-
augmented generation (RAG) to provide cited answers from your research
papers and documents, and works with local models (Ollama) or cloud APIs
(OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, and others).
RAG Assistant for Zotero v0.6.0
- Large libraries now index without running out of memory. Libraries with
  millions of text passages could push the backend past 50 GB and get it shut
  down. The keyword index now lives on disk and updates as you index. (#86,
  reported by @kdbreck)
- Long books index again. Very long PDFs that failed with a "batch size" error
  are now added in parts. (#86)
- Fixed: Sync Metadata stamped every passage with the first item's title,
  authors and tags. If you used Sync Metadata on v0.4.7 or later, run a full
  reindex once after updating.
- Indexing progress now reaches 100%. Scanned PDFs without a text layer are
  listed as skipped instead of stalling the progress bar.
- The app now works when port 8000 is already in use by another program.
- Clearer error messages throughout, and changing profile or embedding model is
  blocked while indexing runs instead of disrupting it.
- Backend logs are now kept in a logs folder in the app's data directory, which
  makes problems much easier to report.
- Security: updated to Electron 44 (Chromium 152). External links opened from
  the app are limited to web addresses.
- macOS 13 (Ventura) or later is now required on Mac, and Linux packages now
  configure the Chromium sandbox correctly on Ubuntu 24.04.
- Updating is automatic — the app will offer v0.6.0 on next launch. Homebrew users
  can run brew upgrade --cask rag-assistant-for-zotero.
